Task Manager — Feature Screenshots

A walkthrough of the main features of the Task Manager app.

1Header with "All Tasks" Button

The top header bar shows the app name "Task Manager" on the left and an "All Tasks" navigation link on the right that returns you to the full task list from any page.

2Filter Task Bar

A filter bar lets you narrow the task list by status. You can switch between All, To Do, In Progress, and Done, with the active filter highlighted in purple.

3Add a Task

The "Add a task" form collects a required Title, an optional Description, and lets you set the initial Status and Priority before adding the task to the list. The "Add Task" button is disabled if the "Title" field is not filled.

4Task List

The task list shows every task as a card with its title, a status badge (Todo / In-Progress / Done), a priority badge (Low / Medium / High), and a Delete button. A counter above shows how many tasks are visible.

5Deleting a Task

Each task card includes a Delete button (highlighted in red here) that removes that task from the list.

6Viewing a Task

Clicking a task opens its detail view, showing the full title, status and priority badges, the complete description, and an Edit button. A "Back to tasks" link returns to the list.

7Editing a Task

The edit view presents the task in an editable form where the Title, Description, Status, and Priority can be changed. Save applies the changes and Cancel discards them.

8Persistence with localStorage

The task list is saved in the browser under the localStorage key "taskManager.tasks". Because the data lives in localStorage, the tasks persist and survive a browser refresh rather than resetting on reload.
